Combine the notes into one sequence. The candle comes before the oak, and the mirror comes after the oak.

source.story: The expedition leaves at dawn, but the mapmaker’s cabinet is locked. Its contents are needed to chart the next route. Across the desk lie seven labeled specimens and keepsakes, scattered during the packing. The oak label belongs to a small wood sample; the star label belongs to a brass token. Beside them is a note: “Restore my collection to its numbered places, first through seventh. Read the first letter of each label in that order, then enter the instrument’s English name.” Use the surviving arrangement notes to open the cabinet.
source.title: The Mapmaker’s Cabinet

hints: Antes y después se refieren a las posiciones numeradas, no al orden en que aparecen ahora las tarjetas.

El orden completo es Botella, Reloj, Útil náutico, Jarra, Uva, Libro, Ancla. Conserva la tilde de Ú al leer las iniciales.

target.story: La expedición parte al amanecer, pero el armario del cartógrafo está cerrado. Su contenido es necesario para trazar la próxima ruta. Sobre el escritorio hay siete muestras y recuerdos etiquetados que quedaron esparcidos durante los preparativos. Una de las etiquetas identifica un útil náutico; otra, un ancla en miniatura. Junto a ellos hay una nota: «Devuelve mi colección a sus lugares numerados, del primero al séptimo. Lee la primera letra de cada etiqueta en ese orden e introduce el nombre del instrumento en español». Usa las notas de colocación que se conservaron para abrir el armario.
target.title: El armario del cartógrafo

notesText: This Spanish adaptation replaces all seven source referents: Candle → Botella, Oak → Reloj, Mirror → Útil náutico, Pear → Jarra, Apple → Uva, Star → Libro, and Shell → Ancla. These are newly authored inventory choices, not literal translations. The seven stable card IDs, all six typed ordering clues, and first-letter extraction are preserved. In the solved order, the replacement labels spell BRÚJULA, matching the Spanish required action. The accented Ú is essential; normalization preserves accents. The target labels were unlocked using “Freeze these labels” for editing and frozen again afterward. The story now describes the replacement collection without revealing its order, and the hints use the new labels, including singular “Útil náutico” to agree with the clue wording. The English source remains unchanged.
